author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A novel about emigration from an overcrowded Earth via a one-way teleport to the colony world Whale's Mouth, and the man who suspects the utopian propaganda conceals something monstrous—expanded years later into a hallucinatory second half; its full form appeared as Lies, Inc. in 1983.
page_summary:
Earth is choked with population, and a corporation offers relief through instantaneous teleportation to the distant colony of Whale's Mouth—a one-way trip, since the ships that could bring anyone back take eighteen years. Rachmael ben Applebaum distrusts the glowing broadcasts from the colony and undertakes the long physical voyage to see for himself whether the promised paradise is real, or a trap concealed behind manufactured images. What he risks discovering is that the whole emigration is a lie masking a sinister purpose.

The book joins Dick's persistent suspicion of official reality: propaganda images stand in for a world no one can independently verify, and the 'utopia' may be a controlled fiction. In the expanded version Dick added a long, drug-and-hallucination-saturated section in which the narrative reality itself fractures, pulling the emigration plot into his characteristic reality breakdown, so that the question of what waits at Whale's Mouth becomes inseparable from the question of what is real at all.

Originally published in a shorter form in the 1960s, the novel had a complicated life; Dick's later, fuller version—with the interpolated hallucinatory material restored—was issued as Lies, Inc. The 1983 edition brought the expanded text to print after his death.
